title: Meta
summary: Today, we are studying a company whose products are used by more humans than any other company in history—Meta—of course, formerly known as Facebook. Meta has four billion monthly active users. Ben: In the over 20 years since its founding, Meta truly has connected humanity through its apps—Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and now Threads.

thesis: This episode argues that Meta's enduring success stems from Mark Zuckerberg's singular, genius-level control over a culture that acts like water, allowing the company to pivot and iterate rapidly against competitors. The thesis posits that this founder-driven flexibility, combined with a history of making multiple successful bets, has consistently neutralized threats and created novel profit centers. Ultimately, the argument is that Meta remains a 'Mark production' where his relentless product strategy and intelligence serve as the primary lever for the company's growth.

claims.claim: The company moves like water, connects the world, and will always gear up for the next battle, whether defining computing, creating AI, or fending off TikTok.
claims.quote: Ultimately, my big takeaway is the company moves like water. It is the company that has connected the world, that will always gear up for the next battle and be whatever they need to be in the next era. Whether it’s them defining the next generation of computing or creating all these AI experiences or fending off the next TikTok or the current TikTok, they just move like water.

claims.claim: Facebook was not really interested in recruiting industry veterans, especially on the technical side.

claims.claim: Facebook became less valuable after the Cambridge Analytica scandal and subsequent privacy issues, wiping out $119 billion in market value in a single day.
claims.quote: Facebook becomes a lot less valuable after all of this comes out. The company announces in their July 2018 earnings call that they’re going to be more focused on user privacy, and that revenue may slow as they make this intense focus. They dropped 19% in one day. They wiped out $119 billion in market value which was the largest single day loss for any company in history at that time.
